newsitem.title: USA: Florida teachers seek guaranteed funding amendment.
newsitem.headline: Florida teachers seek guaranteed funding amendment.

text.p: Florida's teacher unions expect to have ballot language drafted this weekend on a proposed constitutional amendment requiring the state to spend at least 39 percent of its total budget on edcuation, FEA-United President Pat Tornillo said Tuesday.
He said the unions hoped to begin collecting voter signatures during the November general election. It would take 429,428 signatures to force a referendum.
"We're looking at 1998," Tornillo said, adding that the two-year time frame would allow plenty of time to educate voters.
Florida's two teacher unions, FEA-United and FTP-NEA, have hired attorney and former state House Speaker Jon Mills to help draft the ballot language.

"We frankly did not have any confidence or faith that tax reform would ever really be taken up by the Florida Legislature," Tornillo said. "If if this doesn't work then I don't see any hope for public education in Florida."

In fiscal 1986, the state devoted 61 percent of its general tax dollars to public schools. But after voters approved the lottery in 1986, the percentage of tax dollars allocated for education declined steadily, though it rebounded this year to 52 percent, the highest level since 1992.

The trend angered voters who thought the lottery money would be used to enhance education, rather than replace tax funding for schools. At the same time, Florida's school enrollment has grown at more than twice the national rate.
This summer, the state Supreme Court ruled against a lawsuit filed by school districts around the state seeking better funding.
The teachers said 39 percent of the total budget would be equal to about 60 percent of general revenue. The total budget includes federal matching funds, lottery money and trust fund revenues.
